name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries)
tagline: Open daily, including Mondays: lift plus 42 steps to a rooftop view over the compass rose

description.short: Standing 52 meters tall on the Tagus River waterfront, this striking monument celebrates Portugal's Age of Discovery. Designed as a stylized caravel ship with 33 historical figures, it offers panoramic views from its rooftop terrace.
description.full:
The Padrão dos Descobrimentos is the easiest Belém sight to fit into a port day. It is open every day, including Mondays when the Jerónimos Monastery and the Torre de Belém are closed, from 10:00 to 19:00 between March and September and to 18:00 from October to February, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. It stands on the riverfront across the avenue and railway from the monastery; use the underpass by the Praça do Império garden, about 9 minutes' walk.

Much of the value is free. The sculpture group, Henry the Navigator at the prow of a stylised caravel followed by 32 figures of the Discoveries, is on the outside, and the 50-metre compass rose set into the square in front, with a world map tracing Portuguese routes, can be walked over at no cost. The €10 ticket buys the lift to the sixth floor, then 42 narrow steps to the rooftop viewpoint, plus the temporary exhibition. From the top you see the compass rose map properly, the monastery façade, the Torre de Belém to the west and the 25 de Abril Bridge upriver. Allow 30–45 minutes inside.

If time is short, walk round the monument and the compass rose (about 15 minutes) and put the money towards the Jerónimos cloister. If you are skipping the inside of the Torre de Belém, this viewpoint gives you the river panorama without a timed slot. Tickets are sold on site and online through BOL, the only authorised online seller. From here, the tower is about 12 minutes' walk west along the river and MAAT about 16 minutes east.

The monument was built in 1960 for the 500th anniversary of Henry the Navigator's death, replacing a temporary version from the 1940 Portuguese World Exhibition, and it reflects the Estado Novo regime's view of history.
description.history: The first Padrão was a temporary structure of iron, cement and plaster built for the 1940 Portuguese World Exhibition, designed by the architect Cottinelli Telmo and the sculptor Leopoldo de Almeida. The permanent version, in concrete clad with rose-tinted Leiria stone and with figures in Sintra limestone, was built in 1960 to mark 500 years since the death of Henry the Navigator. The compass rose in front, designed by Luís Cristino da Silva and given by South Africa, was inaugurated on 5 August 1960. The interior viewpoint, auditorium and exhibition hall only opened in 1985.
description.significance: The Padrão is less a historic monument than a statement of how the Estado Novo dictatorship wanted the Discoveries remembered, and the monument's own educational programme now presents it in that light. Its 33 figures include navigators such as Vasco da Gama and Pedro Álvares Cabral alongside missionaries, chroniclers, cartographers and the poet Camões. For a visitor, the rooftop is the best place to read Belém's layout: monastery, tower and river in one view.

directions.general: Located on the Belém waterfront between Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower, directly on the Tagus River
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.5 km west on the Belém riverfront. Taxi 15-20 minutes, tram 15E from Praça do Comércio towards Belém, or the train from Cais do Sodré to Belém; the monument is across the road from the Jerónimos Monastery via an underpass.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to Belém. Buses 727, 28, 729, 714, 751. Train to Belém station then 10-minute walk along waterfront.
directions.parking: Public parking available at Praça do Império nearby and along Avenida Brasilia

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open every day except five holidays

admissionPrices.notes: €10 covers the viewpoint, exhibition and film. Youth 13–25 €5 and seniors 65+ €8.50 (non-residents of Lisbon municipality). Children under 12 free. Lisboa Card holders free. Lisbon residents free on Sundays and holidays until 14:00. Online tickets only through BOL.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 30–45 minutes inside; 15 minutes for the exterior and compass rose
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Early morning or late afternoon for best light and fewer crowds. Sunset offers spectacular views from the viewpoint.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Combine with the Jerónimos Monastery (underpass, about 9 minutes) and the Torre de Belém (about 12 minutes west along the river). The compass rose is best seen from the viewpoint above. The film on the monument's construction is shown on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays at 11:15 and 16:00.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2–2.5 hours return from the ship for the monument and viewpoint; it fits easily alongside the Jerónimos Monastery
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Stairs at the entrance (stair-climber for manual wheelchairs on request); lift to floor 6 and the exhibition, but the viewpoint is reached only by 42 narrow steps.
tips: Open every day, including Mondays: the best Belém plan B when the Jerónimos Monastery and the Torre de Belém are closed.
Cross from the monastery through the underpass by the Praça do Império garden (about 9 minutes' walk).
The €10 ticket covers viewpoint, exhibition and film; the €5 exhibition-only ticket skips the view, which is the main reason to go in on a short call.
The lift only goes to the 6th floor; the last 42 steps are a narrow staircase, and the viewpoint wall is 1.30 m high (periscopes are available at reception).
Lisboa Card holders enter free; visitors aged 13–25 pay €5 and over-65s €8.50 (non-Lisbon residents); under-12s free.
Look at the compass rose from the top first, then walk across it to find the routes and dates marked in the stone.
Last entry is 30 minutes before closing: 18:30 from March to September, 17:30 from October to February.
The film on the monument's construction screens at 11:15 and 16:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays.

highlights: Henry the Navigator at the prow, followed by 32 figures of the Discoveries
50 m compass rose in black and red lioz limestone with a 14 m world map (free)
Rooftop viewpoint: lift to the 6th floor, then 42 steps
Views of the Jerónimos Monastery, the Torre de Belém and the 25 de Abril Bridge
Temporary exhibition on floor -1, included in the ticket
Film on the monument's construction (weekends and holidays, 11:15 and 16:00)

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Entrance preceded by two flights of stairs (9 and 6 steps); a stair-climber for manual wheelchairs is available on request. Lift to the exhibition (floor -1) and to floor 6, but the viewpoint is reached only by a narrow 42-step staircase. The square and compass rose are level.
